czar.d: a male monarch or emperor (especially of Russia prior to 1917)

czar alexander i.d: the czar of Russia whose plans to liberalize the government of Russia were unrealized because of the wars with Napoleon (1777-1825)

czar alexander ii.d: the son of Nicholas I who, as czar of Russia, introduced reforms that included limited emancipation of the serfs (1818-1881)

czar alexander iii.d: son of Alexander II who was czar of Russia (1845-1894)

czar nicholas i.d: czar of Russia from 1825 to 1855 who led Russia into the Crimean War (1796-1855)

czar peter i.d: czar of Russia who introduced ideas from western Europe to reform the government; he extended his territories in the Baltic and founded St. Petersburg (1682-1725)

czarina.d: the wife or widow of a czar

czarist.d: of or relating to or characteristic of a czar

czaristic.d: of or relating to or characteristic of a czar

czaritza.d: the wife or widow of a czar

czech.d: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia
a native of inhabitant of the Czech Republic
of or relating to Czechoslovakia or its people or their language

czech capital.d: the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic in the western part of the country; a cultural and commercial center since the 14th century

czechoslovak.d: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia

czechoslovakia.d: a former republic in central Europe; divided into Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1993

czechoslovakian.d: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia
of or relating to Czechoslovakia or its people or their language

czerny.d: Austrian virtuoso pianist and composer of many works for the piano; studied with Beethoven and was a teacher of Liszt (1791-1857)
